correctness.rationale: Every orbit of any unary operation on at most d points is periodic after fewer than d iterations with period dividing d!, so negation powers 2d and 2(d+d!) agree, forcing identical deterministic disjunction values. The dynamic table admits both designated 1 and undesignated k at (1,k), independently for distinct compound formulas. A finite family has bounded carrier size; its common witness contradicts characteristic status. Distinct syntactic formulas do not violate function assignment to each formula. Finite checker exhaustively verifies d≤4, but generality follows from orbit proof.

originality.rationale: Full Aldini et al. 2026 three-valued truth table, dynamic semantics, five-valued projection Theorem 8, and conclusions were compared. Avron–Konikowska 2005 full text and Avron–Zamansky survey Theorem 24 were inspected. The survey theorem assumes two truth values; it cannot directly cover the 2026 three-valued operation. General older existential no-finite-matrix precedents do not assert this exact 2026 case. A concrete separation applies uniformly to any finite family, but stronger historical generic coverage remains possible.
residual_risks: The general phenomenon of nondeterministic logics lacking finite ordinary characteristic matrices is established prior art; broad conceptual priority is not claimed.
Two highly relevant older primary articles were only accessible in abstract or partial form, so an unidentified stronger generic impossibility theorem might subsume the present instance.
No independent scientific review was performed.

value.rationale: The source supplies a specific 5-valued deterministic refinement and emphasizes computational interpretation. The finding rules out every exact finite deterministic characterization, providing explicit bounded-carrier distinguishing sequents. It is substantive relative to the natural finite-semantics question for a new three-valued logic, while acknowledging general old precedents.
